posts.description:
With this film, I won the hackathon at Neulandpro Connect. 🏆
It was made in just under 3.5 hours in CapCut.

The challenge: What does the “Neuland human” look like, and what kind of world do they live in? In other words, the human being after the AI transformation.

The idea: At some point, generative AI will create new realities in real time. In a dystopian, bleak Berlin, life is only bearable through a kind of permanent Instagram filter. Voice-controlled contact lenses reshape reality on command.

I haven’t changed anything in the film since. This is exactly the version that was screened as the winning film at the end of the conference.

A lot of people asked me why the language switches to German at the end. There are two possible explanations:

1. The film is set in Berlin. These days I already speak English here more often than German, but I talk to myself in German, just like the protagonist at the end. So the switch is simply a faithful reflection of reality.
2. During generation, the languages in the prompts got mixed up, and under the time pressure there was no chance to fix it.
3. First 2. happened, and then 1. followed from it.

For the non-German speakers: She says, “I wish I could go back to the moment before everything turned to shit.”

Pick your favorite. 😉

#AI #GenerativeAI #AIFilm #Hackathon #NeulandProConnect #CapCut #Filmmaking #Berlin #Dystopia

Huge thanks to Neulandpro, AI Filmmakers Berlin and with this Ben Chimoy, the jury Sylvia Nitzsche, Esther Gronenborn, Shamila Lengsfeld, Adrian Daniel Botnariu, Seb Ungrad, Phil Langer and of course CapCut for the credits and the great support throughout the hackathon. 💻

posts.transcript: OpenAI���s internal research system resolve the Navier Stokes Millennium prize problem.  GPT 6 Astra completed the lean formalization and verification. It made me think about a much more familiar problem. Why is natural movement so difficult to recreate? You see it in games, animation and robotics. Our model can have the right shape, the right joints, even the right poses and still move in a way that feels mechanical. Natural movement is not a sequence of static poses, it is a coupled dynamic system rhythm flowing through geometry. Good OpenAI���s mathematical intelligence over a novel way to create movement. That was the experiment behind forma Could GPT 6 take the periodic rhythms we see in nature, express them through harmonic components and build a live motion system around them? So I built Forma, an embodied motion optimization engine using procedural generation. Look at these examples. The fish moves through periodic body wave, traveling from head to tail. The snake uses a similar travelling wave, but its phase relationship with the ground creates forward propulsion. The salamander has to coordinate a body wave with contact constraints. Feet land, hold, release and step again. And the jellyfish moved through a periodic pulse contraction release drift. Different animals, different mechanics, but the underlying language is remarkably consistent. Periodic motion, harmonic structure, and geometric constraint. For the periodic part of a movement, Fourier decomposition gives us a powerful way to think. A complex rhythm can be expressed as a combination of simple sine waves. The fundamental frequency establishes the cadence. Harmonics add the nuance, curvature, acceleration, asymmetry, and the subtle timing that makes your body feel alive. Amplitude determines how far the body moves, frequency determines how quickly it moves, phase determines how different parts move together, and spatial wavelength determines how that motion travels across the body. You can picture every sine wave as the shadow of a point rotating around the circle. Combine circles, combine harmonics, and rich motion emerges from simple ingredients. Now I'm asking it to animate a manta ray using more mobuliform locomotion. Manta does not swim like a fish. It's large pectoral fins perform broad dorsoventral oscillations, like wings flying through water. Watch the system build it GPT 6 Astra researches the motion, identifies the rays, shape, kinematic primitives and constrained structure, then constructs the creature. Live anchors establish the frame distance constraints preserve the body's segment lengths. Chain constraints distribute the bending. The silhouette emerges, the pectoral fins attach, then harmonic motion begins to drive the rig. And now the manta swims. The fundamental oscillation creates the wing beat, higher harmonics shape the fin curvature and timing constraints reserve the rays form as the motion flows through it. This is forma - motion from Imagination with GPT 6 Astra.
posts.description:
🏆 Forma, my OpenAI GPT-6 Astra project, was selected as the Best build at Astra Commons London. 🏆

Why is natural motion so difficult to recreate?
That was the problem I wanted to explore with Forma.

OpenAI’s Navier–Stokes result, where GPT-6 Astra completed the Lean formalisation and verification, got me thinking about whether its advanced mathematical reasoning could help solve a very different kind of problem: recreating natural motion (mathematically)

Forma uses GPT-6 Astra to investigate Fourier-inspired procedural locomotion, drawing on periodic signals, harmonic relationships, phase, and geometric constraints to shape movement.

There’s plenty more to improve, but the first examples are ready to explore:
🔗 Try Forma: https://lnkd.in/easDQY-H

🎥 Full video: https://lnkd.in/ekEq7fYF

A huge thank you to Andy Tyler for organising Astra Commons London and for the additional Codex credits, and to Oscar Falemara and Pauline P. Narvas for being part of the team that made it happen.

And thank you to everyone who attended Astra Commons London. It was great meeting you all, exchanging ideas, and connecting with so many talented people. Looking forward to staying in touch

posts.description:
Google just let 10 AI crews run their own indie film hackathon. What were the takeaways?

1️⃣ Agents collaborate better through files, not messages: Whenever agents crashed or ran out of context window and restarted, they lost their chat history. The teams that succeeded passed messages containing file paths rather than raw instructions.

2️⃣ Choose styles that match AI limitations: The best films didn't fight AI's limitations: they embraced them. For example, they chose claymation because the natural "wobble" made video drift invisible.

3️⃣ Specificity always beats general direction: "Make it warm" or "cinematic" produced generic cinematic noir. The winning teams used precise parameters like hex color codes and wrote negative prompts.

4️⃣ An "Editor-in-Chief" is needed: Each crew had three specialized roles: the Idea Person, the Technical Lead, and the Editor. A Coach Agent couldn't write or edit, but they were essential to enforce quality after each step.

Read the full writeup from Preston Holmes and G. Hussain Chinoy in the comments.

posts.description:
Google's Gemini 4 Argon is now available for everyone.

To test the model's spatial reasoning and visual coding capabilities, Geneviève Huskens generated a playable 3D racing game, "Desk Racer," directly from photos of her desk.

Here's the workflow she documented:
→ Planning: Used /grill-me in Antigravity to define the track mechanics and scale before writing 3D code.
→ Multi-agent execution: Set a /goal command where Argon orchestrated subagents across Blender MCP and Three.js.
→ Collision math: Computed surface intersections so all 68 track pillars aligned with the desk surface and objects without clipping.
→ Shaders and textures: Used Nano Banana for asset texturing alongside Three.js shaders and audio synthesis.

In this video, I take the game for a test drive in Google AI Studio. You can switch between chase, cockpit, and drone camera views as you navigate around physical desk items like a mechanical keyboard and microphone.

The demo is available to play directly in Google AI Studio, and Geneviève published a technical walkthrough detailing the build process. Links are in the first comment.

fal is an official launch partner for OpenAI's new role-specific plugins in Codex, going live today.

The bigger shift worth flagging: agents are becoming the surface where creative work actually happens, not just where it gets discussed. With fal in Codex, teams can bring models, assets, and workflows from fal directly into Codex sessions, so analysis, prototyping, creative review, and reporting stay in one place instead of fragmenting across tabs and tools.

For creative production teams, that closes the gap between a brief and a useful output. For organizations standardizing on Codex for role-specific workflows, it makes fal's generative infrastructure available exactly where the work is being done.

posts.description:
Every company at LA Tech Week has had a little (AI) work done.

You can tell. The demos are shiny/animated, the presos are rendered in flawless HTML, and everyone is sharing their favorite grokbot implementation.

Then there’s the stat I keep bringing up: Accenture found 90% of organizations have moved to implement AI, and nearly half of tech leaders say their company has yet to redesign a single role.

In LA we have a word for that. It’s filler. Great lighting, looks amazing from across the room, and underneath it’s the same org chart running the same workflows out of the same scattered inboxes and spreadsheets.

The real glow-up takes more work, and it’s a lot more fun:
- Put the whole business somewhere AI can actually read it: CRM, ERP, email, the shared drive from 2019, and everything that only lives in your COO’s head.
- Map every workflow and decide what the agents run and what your people own.
- Rebuild the roles around that, and keep tuning.
- Do that and a 20-person firm starts doing what used to take 200.

LA runs on companies that size: production houses, PR agencies, law firms, the manufacturers out in Commerce and Vernon. They have the most to gain, because they can move in weeks while the giants are still scheduling the steering committee.

#LATechWeek #AI

posts.transcript: This is a quick demo of kind of AD sandboxes. So as Astra continues to improve on being able to go from, you know, a prompt to CAD models effectively, I expect to kind of see the same shift that we saw with tournaments where we migrated out of the ID and into kind of background terminal UI as well as like asynchronous background agents. So what I put together is basically a WS environment workstation VMS that deploys Fusion 360, lets you log in and then let's Codex connect. Lead to that be a kind of a rapper server interface, so it exposes all of the traditional CAD commands that you might want and then exposes the live model view through kind of a terminal browser UI. So that way you can basically see both codecs on the left and then the models on the right essentially. And then the final piece of this is basically a browser automation flow where we take the model that was just designed and then script around kind of. Supplier work websites, is that what you need? Get your model shipped to you directly. It fills up all the forms, uses the link CLI to complete payment and then ships it directly to you. So this is kind of an end to end flow as we see you know more people get exposed to kind of CAD design capabilities as Codex continues to improve and and Astra continues to improve.
posts.description:
I competed in OpenAI's first onsite hackathon to celebrate the GPT-6/Astra launch and took 1st place, winning $50k and tickets to Dev Day 2026. 

Over the past 9 months I've been exploring and working with the different frontier models to understand their understanding of the 3D world across CAD, CAM and manufacturing of different woodworking and 3D printed projects.

One thing that stuck out with the latest Astra release was how much its understanding of CAD has improved. This provided a perfect opportunity to explore what a CAD sandbox might look like in the same way we have coding sandboxes. 

I took Fusion 360, put it on an AWS Workstation VM and wrapped the SDK with a server that allowed Codex to remotely interact with, stream and modify models straight from the terminal. Then we took the live stream and exposed it via a terminal in the browser so you could both interact with Codex and see what it was working on with all the compute running in the background. 

We saw coding shift from Tab to Agent to Background Agents as capabilities improved and longer horizon tasks became possible. CAD sandboxes is base on the same bet that as models are able to act autonomously for longer, compute shifts into the background to enable use cases.
